analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md. The only changed range is line 2126, a documentation edit describing the `stop` parameter and its reasoning/tool-call exclusion scopes. That line lies outside the two supplied excerpts (lines 420-1216), which are unchanged surrounding documentation, so I found no new behavior in them. I read the excerpts against the threat model anyway.

Prefix cache: the Nemotron Super checkpoints are encrypted SSD checkpoints scoped by the coordinator-authenticated cache scope and off without one. This matches the T-041 posture (HMAC-keyed names, scope folded into the tag, 30-minute TTL, KEK-wipe purge, SEC-035 as an accepted risk). The text also says a durable checkpoint's identity rests on pinned shard SHA-256 and the prompt-contract hash, and that a post-load hash mismatch refuses the load. It makes no TTL, name-derivation or scope-isolation change that would need a fresh SEC-035 sign-off.

Image requests: without a scope they stay cold and never publish, and image checkpoints have no durable layout.

General: the other described behaviors are availability and admission controls, such as 429/503 refusals, memory-claim fitting and wedge retirement. They are consistent with T-010, T-016 and T-029. They claim no runtime secrecy beyond the existing model (T-056).

The documented stop-scope change at line 2126 is about correct string matching. It is a doc-only change with no visible security regression. Remaining integration question: whether the described `ReasoningStopScope` behavior matches the code. That is outside the supplied evidence and is a correctness matter, not a security one.
